rules.statement: Every path that hashes or verifies a password must use the NFC (Unicode Normalization Form C) form of the password through one shared IPasswordHasher<TUser> decorator, so that the library's own code and the host's ASP.NET Core Identity pages (CreateAsync, ChangePasswordAsync, ResetPasswordAsync, CheckPasswordAsync) hash and verify the same form.
rules.why: If one path hashes the NFC form and another hashes the password as typed, a password that is not in NFC stops working at one of them once the other has stored or replaced its hash.
rules.check: Look for password hashing or verification that skips the normalizing hasher, for example a direct PasswordHasher<TUser> or a raw hasher call, or that hashes the password as typed while another path hashes its NFC form.

rules.statement: When a normalizing password hasher fails to verify the NFC form and the NFC form differs from the provided password, verify the provided password as well and report a match as PasswordVerificationResult.SuccessRehashNeeded.
rules.why: Hashes stored earlier from the typed form keep verifying, and UserManager replaces them with a hash of the NFC form.
rules.check: Look at VerifyHashedPassword in a normalizing decorator: it must fall back to the provided form only when the NFC form differs, and that fallback must return SuccessRehashNeeded, not Success.

rules.statement: When normalizing a password, treat a string that string.Normalize refuses (for example one with an unpaired surrogate) as having no normal form and use it as provided, instead of throwing.
rules.why: A password with an unpaired surrogate has no NFC form, and the hash and verify paths must still handle it the same way every time.
rules.check: Look for string.Normalize calls on password input with no handling for the ArgumentException thrown for invalid UTF-16, or handling that differs between the hash path and the verify path.

rules.statement: A DI extension that decorates a service the framework registers with TryAdd must work in either registration order: replace the last non-keyed registration in place with one of the same lifetime that wraps its instance, factory or implementation type, and if there is none, register the decorator around the default implementation so that the later TryAdd leaves it in place.
rules.why: The host may register its implementation before or after the library call, and TryAdd keeps an earlier registration while a later one wins, so the decorator has to apply either way.
rules.check: Look for decorator registrations that only append a new descriptor, change the lifetime, handle only implementation-type descriptors and not instance or factory ones, or break when the framework's TryAdd runs after them.

rules.statement: A decorator registration or factory must not wrap an inner service that is already an instance of the same decorator.
rules.why: Wrapping twice would apply the decorator's transformation, such as normalization, twice.
rules.check: Look in decorator wrapping code for a missing 'inner is TDecorator' check before wrapping.

rules.statement: Keep a transformation such as password normalization in one implementation (the decorator). Consumers should require that decorator and throw an InvalidOperationException whose message names the fix when it is missing, not repeat the transformation themselves.
rules.why: With one implementation, every path takes the same normalization steps, and a misconfigured host gets an actionable error instead of quietly behaving differently.
rules.check: Look for consumers that normalize passwords themselves, or that accept any hasher without checking that it is the normalizing decorator, or that throw without telling the developer how to fix it.

rules.statement: Check for a required service that may depend on request-scoped services when it is used, not when the host starts. Only operations that actually use it should throw.
rules.why: A service such as a password hasher can need request services, so it cannot be built before a request, and operations that don't need it (such as a create without a password) should not fail.
rules.check: Look for startup validation that resolves request-dependent services from the root provider, or for checks that throw on code paths that never use the service.

rules.statement: Make a dummy password hash, used to equalize timing for unknown accounts, with the same normalizing hasher that verifies real hashes, and verify it through that hasher.
rules.why: The dummy then takes the same steps as a stored hash, so a password that is not in NFC costs the same number of verifications whether or not the account exists.
rules.check: Look for dummy hashes made with a different hasher instance or type, or verified by a path that is not the one used for real accounts.

rules.statement: When a stored password hash is replaced only to upgrade its form (a rehash of the same credential), keep the user's security stamp.
rules.why: The credential has not changed, so sessions and tokens tied to the security stamp should stay valid.
rules.check: Look for rehash-on-verify code that calls UpdateSecurityStampAsync or rotates the stamp when the password itself did not change.
